issues.legal_issue: A purchaser claiming through a party to a pending property-title suit is not a necessary or proper party when the dispute can be fully adjudicated between the existing parties and the purchaser has no independent ground to contest the title on which the suit is based.
material_facts: The suit sought a declaration of ownership founded on a registered will.
An earlier decree, which had become final, had adjudicated a claim based on the same will after one of the testator’s daughters was made a party.
While the later suit was pending, the defendants sold the disputed property to the proposed parties.
The purchasers claimed through heirs of the daughter who had been a party to the earlier suit, and their asserted title did not give them a ground to challenge the will.
issues.conclusion: The purchasers were neither necessary nor proper parties, and the application to implead them was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 1, Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure, a necessary party is one whose presence is indispensable to effective and complete adjudication; a proper party is one whose presence is needed for effective and complete adjudication of the dispute. The court applied those tests to the purchasers’ derivative claim and the final earlier adjudication of the will. It held that New Redbank Tea Co. Pvt. Ltd. v. Kumkum Mittal and Ramesh H. Kundanmal v. Municipal Corporation of Greater Bombay did not apply to these facts.

predicates.property_title_declaration_suit: The proceeding seeks a determination of title to property.
predicates.purchaser_claims_through_party_to_suit: The proposed party claims an interest derived from a person who is already a party to the proceeding.
predicates.existing_parties_can_fully_litigate_disp: The dispute can be effectively and completely adjudicated between the parties already before the court.
predicates.purchaser_has_no_independent_ground_to_c: The proposed party’s asserted interest supplies no independent ground to contest the title basis relied on in the proceeding.
predicates.purchaser_not_necessary_or_proper_party: The proposed party is neither necessary nor proper for adjudication of the proceeding.

issues.definition: When a title-declaration proceeding can be fully decided between the existing parties and a derivative purchaser has no independent ground to contest its title basis, the purchaser is not needed as a party.

issues.legal_issue: A transfer of property by a party while a non-collusive suit directly and specifically concerns rights in that property, made without the court’s authority, is subject to the rights determined by the decree and does not affect those rights.
material_facts: The suit directly and specifically concerned rights in the disputed property.
While the suit was pending, defendants transferred the property to the proposed parties by registered sale deeds.
The transfers were not made with the authority of the court.
issues.conclusion: The transfers were hit by the doctrine of lis pendens and were subject to the rights determined in the suit; the purchasers’ transfers did not make them necessary or proper parties.
issues.legal_principle: Section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act provides that during the pendency of a non-collusive suit or proceeding in which rights to immovable property are directly and specifically in question, a party cannot transfer or otherwise deal with the property so as to affect another party’s rights under a decree or order, except with the court’s authority and on its terms.

predicates.non_collusive_property_rights_suit_pendi: A non-collusive suit or proceeding directly and specifically concerning rights in property is pending.
predicates.party_transfers_property_in_dispute: A party to the proceeding transfers or otherwise deals with the property in dispute while the proceeding is pending.
predicates.transfer_without_court_authority: The party makes the transfer without obtaining the court’s authority.
predicates.transfer_subject_to_rights_under_decree: The transfer remains subject to the rights determined by the decree and does not affect those rights.

issues.definition: When a party transfers disputed property without court authority during a pending non-collusive property-rights proceeding, the transfer remains subject to the rights determined in the proceeding.
